edit.description: `skillDefaultContract` (~1306+) carries no `mentionReachable` clause; `ruleDefaultContract` does (line 1508, `clause(mentionReachable("paths", "paths"), {...})`). Add the equivalent clause to `skillDefaultContract` so a skill consulting a narrower-gated member is flagged the same way a rule is.
Regression: skillDefaultContract carries the mention-reachable clause.
Frozen built-in lock snapshot shifts with the new clause; regenerate.

summary: Add mentionReachable("paths","paths") to skillDefaultContract, matching ruleDefaultContract — a skill's narrower-gated mention currently goes unflagged.

tests.asserts: skillDefaultContract includes a mentionReachable(paths, paths) clause

acceptance: A skill mentioning a member whose gate doesn't contain the skill's own scope is flagged, the same as a rule is today.
notes: GH #36, human-ruled 09-03. Explicitly blockedBy #33's fix — landing this first, over today's literal-containment leniency, would multiply the false positive onto skill members. scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: New sibling check beside `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` (which 21f61463 added for two *kinds* sharing one collectionAddress): a *single* kind's own members registering on the same key within that address (e.g. three `hook` members on `SessionStart`, which collapse to one entry in the `kind:name` composition map — silent last-writer-wins) is a declaration-time refusal with a named error, not a silent collapse.
Wire the new diagnostic beside the existing `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` call (~gate.rs:200s).
Regression: three hook members declared on the same event refuse loud, naming all colliding members — mirroring 21f61463's kind-collision test shape.

summary: Refuse a duplicate member registration key within one kind's collection address (three hooks on SessionStart collapse to one) with a named error, not last-writer-wins.

tests.asserts: duplicate hook members on the same event name are refused loud, naming both

acceptance: Two `hook` members declared on the same `event` refuse at declaration time with a named error rather than silently composing to whichever was last.
notes: GH #32, human-ruled 09-03. Same disease 21f61463 refused for two kinds sharing one collectionAddress; this is the narrower case of one kind's own members colliding on the same key. Whether hook also grows an address discriminator is a follow-on fork to surface, not to invent here. scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: `member_projection_path` (~911) resolves an `at`-locus member (governs_root + governs_glob present together) to a path under the given root with no check that the root avoids the workspace. Refuse at `emit` (in `emit()`'s member loop, ~1206+) when an `at` locus's root falls under `WORKSPACE_DIR`, with a named error — it would emit and lock but never be discoverable.

Companion check-time refusal reading the committed lock's row for an `at`-locus member whose `source_path` falls under `.temper/` — the same invariant enforced on the already-committed state, not only at the next emit.
Wire the new check-time diagnostic beside the other admissibility calls.
Regression: an `at` locus declared under `.temper/` refuses at emit and at check, naming the offending path.

summary: Refuse an `at` locus rooted under the workspace, at emit and at check: it currently emits and locks but discovery fences .temper/ by design, so it's silently unreachable.

tests.asserts: an at locus under .temper/ refuses at emit and at check with a named error

acceptance: An `at` locus whose root resolves under the workspace directory is refused at emit and flagged at check on an already-committed lock row; discovery's own WORKSPACE_DIR fence is unchanged.
notes: GH #30, human-ruled 09-03. src/import.rs:439's discoverable_paths already fences WORKSPACE_DIR by design for every non-local walk (verified on disk); the gap is that emit/check never refuse the declaration that produces an undiscoverable target — discovery does not change, the workspace stays authoring source, never a projection target. blockedBy HOOK-COLLECTION-ADDRESS-DUPLICATE-REFUSAL only for the shared src/admissibility.rs + src/gate.rs region. scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: `guard()` (~732) and `matches_projection` (~819) bind `file_path` against `drift::EmitOwnedEntry` targets; `.claude/settings.json` is the spliced projection of every `hook`/`installed-plugin`/`known-marketplace` member but is not itself an `EmitOwnedEntry` row (it's composed, not projected whole), so every spelling of it is currently silent to the guard. Extend the bound target set to cover `settings.json` as an emit-owned target whenever any of those kinds compose. Also state plainly, in `GUARD_MESSAGE` (~160) and the guard's doc comments, that the guard binds only `Write`/`Edit`/`MultiEdit`-mediated writes (`GUARD_MATCHER`, ~136) and is not a boundary against Bash/PowerShell-mediated writes.

`emit_owned_targets` (~2968) is the constituency the guard binds to; verify the settings.json coverage against 0034's emit codomain so the covered-target set has one home rather than a second definition in install.rs.
Regression: a pending write to .claude/settings.json is bound by the guard; a Bash-tool payload is documented as unbound, not silently treated as covered.

summary: Extend temper guard's target set to .claude/settings.json (spliced from hook/installed-plugin/known-marketplace members) and document its Bash-write boundary plainly.

tests.asserts: a PreToolUse payload naming .claude/settings.json is bound by the guard when any registration-member kind composes

acceptance: A pending Write/Edit/MultiEdit to .claude/settings.json is bound by temper guard whenever a hook/installed-plugin/known-marketplace member projects into it; the guard's own docs state plainly it binds tool-mediated writes only.
notes: GH #38 half 1 + half 2a, human-ruled 09-03. Half 2b (a PostToolUse Bash arm) is filed as its own entry, blockedBy this one for the shared install.rs guard region. This entry is itself blockedBy REQUIREMENT-KIND-CONSTRAINT-ENFORCEMENT for the shared src/drift.rs region (transitively serialized behind the admissibility.rs/gate.rs cluster). scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: The `PreToolUse` guard (`GUARD_MATCHER`, ~136: `Write|Edit|MultiEdit`) never sees a Bash/PowerShell-mediated write, and a Bash payload carries no `file_path` to bind against. Add a new `PostToolUse` hook group placement, matcher `Bash`, beside the existing `PreToolUse` guard group's install/converge logic (~1075-1200): it runs after the call and re-checks emit-owned targets for drift (check-style), rather than parsing `tool_input.command` shell text before the call.
Regression: install places/converges a PostToolUse Bash hook group; the hook's command runs drift detection over emit-owned targets, not command-text parsing.

summary: Add a PostToolUse arm on Bash that runs check-style drift detection over emit-owned targets after the call, since the PreToolUse guard cannot see Bash-mediated writes.

tests.asserts: a PostToolUse Bash hook group is placed and re-checks emit-owned targets for drift

acceptance: After a Bash-mediated edit to an emit-owned target, the next PostToolUse Bash call surfaces the resulting drift finding in-band.
notes: GH #38 half 2b, human-ruled 09-03. External fact verified 2026-09-03 (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, fetched this tick): PostToolUse supports a Bash matcher and receives tool_input.command but no file_path — the design re-checks emit-owned targets rather than parsing shell text, so the hook contract poses no blocker; not parked. blockedBy the prior entry only for the shared install.rs guard region. scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: `project_bytes` (~2372) and the `emit()` projection loop (~1054+) currently read banner `placements` only off the *already-committed* file on disk (~2298-2299: "Those metadata lines ride install, never emit") — a member that only ever ran `emit` ships bannerless. Move banner origination here: emit places the managed-projection banner on every target it owns, since it already owns the projected bytes and the banner is part of the projection contract. Verify the double-emit determinism pass and the byte-vs-lock-hash drift comparison both treat the banner as ordinary projection bytes, so an unchanged emit still reports unchanged.

`NOTE_COMMENT`/`NOTE_BANNER`/`project_banner` (~181-1714) currently originate the banner; narrow install's role to converging an existing file's banner wording (a stale wording re-places) rather than being the sole placer for a fresh projection.
Regression: a freshly emitted member (never installed) carries the managed-projection banner.
Regression: install still converges a stale banner wording to current; no double-banner on re-run.

summary: Move the managed-projection banner's placement from install to emit — emit owns the projected bytes, so a member that only ever ran emit should not ship bannerless.

tests.asserts: a member emitted without ever having been installed carries the banner

acceptance: Every emit-owned projection carries the managed-projection banner immediately after emit, with no dependency on install having run first; drift reports no spurious churn from the banner's own placement.
notes: GH #37, human-ruled 09-03. src/drift.rs:2298's own comment currently states the opposite design ("ride install, never emit") — this entry is a deliberate reversal per the ruling, not a bug in that comment's accuracy today. blockedBy the guard entries above only for the shared install.rs file, not a design dependency. scoped at 1466a1db.

edit.description: Satisfier admission (~123) already refuses an unmodeled kind naming a requirement's `kind`, but is otherwise kind-blind: any modeled kind's satisfier fills a requirement regardless of its declared `kind`. Enforce the constraint — a satisfier of a kind other than the requirement's declared `kind` is a required-severity finding on the satisfier.
Requirement admissibility (~104-125) checks `kind` narrows to a *modeled* kind (dead-selector case); this is the sibling live case — a filled requirement whose filler's kind mismatches.
`explain`'s fill listing excludes a wrong-kind satisfier from "filling" the requirement, consistent with the new finding.
Regression: a `kind: skill` requirement filled by an `installed-plugin` satisfier is flagged, and explain does not list it as filling.

summary: Enforce a requirement's declared `kind`: a satisfier of another kind is a required-severity finding, and explain excludes it from filling the requirement.

per.section: requirement — a shipped kind, not a primitive

tests.asserts: a kind-mismatched satisfier is a required-severity finding and is excluded from explain's fill listing

acceptance: A requirement declared `kind: skill` filled only by an `installed-plugin` satisfier now surfaces a required-severity finding naming the mismatch, and `explain` does not credit the fill.
notes: GH #28, human-ruled 09-03. sdk/src/contract.ts:344 already documents `kind` as constraining what may fill a requirement; src/roster.rs already refuses an unmodeled kind, so the seam exists — what's missing is the live mismatch finding. blockedBy AT-LOCUS-WORKSPACE-DISCOVERY-REFUSAL only for the shared src/admissibility.rs region. scoped at 1466a1db.
